card.name: Padjanbel
card.tagline: Gwoka work rhythm tied to sugarcane cutting.
card.profile: Padjanbel (also padjabel, granjanbel, gwadjanbel) is one of the seven gwoka base rhythms, a work rhythm in 3/4 whose jerky movements recall the gestures of enslaved plantation workers, especially the cutting of sugarcane; it is also described as a women's rhythm symbolizing grace, pride and liberation, linking earth and sky. Played on the ka drums (two boula plus make) with chacha and responsorial Creole song, danced in the lawonn at lewoz gatherings (Mulaogwada; Wikipedia: Gwo ka).
card.insight: Padjanbel is the gwoka rhythm most explicitly tied to sugarcane-cutting labor, though some traditions reinterpret it as a warrior dance.
